0 Six-follicle overview.note: Orient to the six representative thyroid follicles, lumen content, retained support and separate parathyroid context. The corner cut is a deliberate display section. The parathyroid corner is a separate comparison sample, not a thyroid follicle or a whole-gland location map. Fine resorption, C-cell and basket details are initially hidden to keep the hierarchy readable.

1 Retained support and vessels.note: Read capsule, septa and interfollicular connective tissue around the retained follicular units and sampled vascular courses. Retained support is already dissected and fitted around delivered vessels and tissue. Its shallow floor, ridge and posterior capsule are teaching context, not a complete closed thyroid capsule. Arterial and venous trunks are sampled courses; the capillary baskets are separate disconnected examples.

2 Follicular wall and colloid.note: Distinguish the one-cell-thick follicular epithelial wall, extracellular colloid lumen and retained basal lamina. The camera targets the nominal front-right follicle before settling; all six units share each part mesh, so this is a camera detail view, not independent isolation of one follicle. Colloid is retained extracellular lumen content. The posterior basal lamina is opaque retained tissue; its missing anterior portion is authored dissection.

3 Basal lamina and capillary baskets.note: Inspect the basal side of the epithelial wall beside retained lamina and representative perifollicular baskets. Turning off the display cut restores only shader-clipped geometry; it does not restore the source-dissection portions. Three baskets sample six follicles. Neutral #99618c preserves their identity without inventing arterial-to-venous connectivity. Iodide supply and hormone transfer are functional explanations, not a depicted continuous flow circuit.

4 Apical colloid resorption.note: Read scalloped colloid and the resorption markers at the epithelial apical interface. The source contains actual radial colloid concavities plus separate pale ellipsoidal resorption markers. Markers identify a teaching location; they are not solid inclusions to carve out or flowing hormone particles. Cellular uptake and processing are narrated because this original model has no separate vesicle or lysosome meshes and no animation.

5 Basal and interfollicular C cells.note: Separate the pale-blue C-cell examples from the colloid-facing follicular epithelium. The source includes basal epithelial C-cell examples and one interfollicular example. Their teaching color identifies the cell class; routine H&E alone may not identify C cells reliably. Preserve their absence of colloid contact. Calcitonin release is toward blood, with no need to import review_v2 signaling symbols or nuclei.

6 Parathyroid comparison sample.note: Compare a separate parathyroid sample containing chief cells, oxyphil cells, adipocytes and a sampled capillary. Thyroid parts are hidden to prevent a false impression of parathyroid colloid or inter-specimen continuity. The posterior half-capsule is retained and its anterior half is already dissected away. Cell counts and cell dimensions are schematic. The single neutral capillary lacks a depicted arterial/venous connection. This is the original context sample, not thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2.

functional_teaching.presentation: Static narrated progression using existing named parts. No added molecule, organelle, arrow, or motion geometry.

steps.caption: The basal vascular side supplies iodide to follicular cells; this sampled geometry does not draw a complete perfusion path.
Follicular cells make thyroglobulin; hormone precursors are formed and stored with it in extracellular colloid.
TSH-stimulated colloid uptake and intracellular processing precede T3/T4 release toward nearby blood vessels; markers do not animate this mechanism.
C cells release calcitonin toward blood without reaching the colloid.
Chief cells in the separate parathyroid context are the PTH-secreting cell class. Oxyphil and fat are identification context, not extra thyroid follicles.

boundaries: No physiological state change is implied by changing teaching presets.
Pre/Post refine compare processing outputs, not low/high gland activity.
Epithelium height and scalloping are illustrative morphology, not a diagnostic result or hormone-production meter.

description_overrides.Follicular epithelium: Simple follicular epithelium facing colloid apically and blood-facing stroma basally. The six teaching units use fewer, enlarged cells. Activity influences epithelial height, but these units are not a calibrated activity or disease atlas. The small geometric clefts separate cell outlines schematically; intact follicles are sealed by epithelial junctions.
description_overrides.Colloid: Colloid is the extracellular thyroglobulin-rich content of the follicular lumen, storing thyroid hormone bound within thyroglobulin. It is drawn as a filled storage domain with named marginal resorption pockets. This is not blood, mucosal tissue or an excretory duct.
description_overrides.Resorption vacuoles: Pale teaching markers identify marginal resorption pockets next to the apical follicular surface. The colloid surface has separately authored concavities at these sites. These markers are not a cell population or intracellular colloid droplets, and their placement is a schematic representation of resorption.
description_overrides.Parafollicular C cells: Calcitonin-secreting C cells are represented basally within some follicular epithelial sectors and by one interfollicular example. Basal examples remain covered by principal cells and do not contact colloid. Precursors enter the thyroid with the ultimobranchial body; modern mouse lineage tracing supports pharyngeal-endoderm origin, replacing the older neural-crest account. Human calcitonin has a limited and incompletely defined role in normal calcium regulation.
description_overrides.Perifollicular capillaries: Three representative hollow capillary baskets illustrate the rich blood supply outside follicular basal surfaces. They represent an exchange bed; endothelial fenestrations are not geometrically resolved. These sampled baskets are not connected to the displayed artery and vein, and the neutral color does not imply arterial or venous identity.
description_overrides.Arteries (capsular & interlobular): Representative arterial course in the dissected capsular/interlobular context. In vivo, arterial branches supply the perifollicular capillary bed. This source depicts a hollow trunk rather than every named arterial origin or the missing connections to its sampled capillary baskets.
description_overrides.Veins (capsular & interlobular): Representative venous course in the dissected capsular/interlobular context. In vivo, thyroid venous channels drain the capillary bed. This source depicts a hollow trunk; the connections from its sampled baskets and all named drainage veins are not shown.
description_overrides.Interfollicular connective tissue: Dissected interfollicular support is represented by a shallow connective-tissue floor fitted around the final follicular, vascular and parathyroid surfaces. The biological stroma also carries lymphatics and nerve fibers; those are not separate illustrated structures in this model.
description_overrides.Interlobular septa: Retained connective-tissue septal context represented by a low ridge fitted around neighboring structures. Biological septa partly partition gland tissue and carry larger vessels. This six-follicle sample does not show a complete lobule or establish a fixed number of follicles per lobule.
description_overrides.Capsule: Retained posterior true-capsule context in a dissected teaching sample. The anterior portion is removed to expose the follicles. This part is not a complete enclosing shell. The external fascial capsule and whole-gland swallowing attachments are contextual anatomy, not illustrated structures here.
description_overrides.Follicular basal lamina: Magnified basal-lamina segments demonstrate the outside of the follicular epithelial layer. The anterior portion is intentionally dissected away. Membrane thickness is exaggerated for teaching; the retained segments do not form a whole-sphere containment host.
description_overrides.Parathyroid capsule: Retained posterior half-capsule of the parathyroid comparison sample. It separates this cell-rich comparison tissue from the thyroid follicles. The sample is count-reduced and is not a physically scaled complete parathyroid gland.
description_overrides.Parathyroid chief cells: Predominant chief-cell examples in the parathyroid comparison sample. They secrete PTH toward nearby blood. Biological parathyroid cells form cords and nests, but this source shows discrete enlarged examples rather than a continuous reconstruction of those cords.
description_overrides.Oxyphil cells: Fewer, larger oxyphil-cell examples distinguish the parathyroid comparison from thyroid follicles. Their conspicuously eosinophilic cytoplasm is mitochondria-rich; their normal functional significance remains incompletely understood. These are enlarged teaching examples.
description_overrides.Parathyroid adipocytes: Three sampled adipocytes show the fatty stromal component of a parathyroid comparison. Their drawn count is schematic and does not assign an age or a fat percentage to the sample.
description_overrides.Parathyroid capillaries: Hollow sampled capillary beside the chief-cell examples, illustrating release of PTH toward blood. This independent course has no depicted arterial or venous connection. Its neutral color does not imply either identity, and endothelial fenestrations are not geometrically resolved.

limitations: Teaching time and glow are schematic; they do not quantify hormones, transport rates, blood flow or biological storage duration.
Exact selectors address aggregate existing parts; this hook cannot identify a single follicular cell or draw an organelle that is absent from the mesh.
The thyroid capillary baskets and arterial/venous trunks are representative disconnected samples. No continuous artery-to-capillary-to-vein tracer route is asserted.
Parathyroid capillaries are a separate representative sample without depicted supply/drainage connections. Thyroid and parathyroid are never one endocrine circuit.
Resorption vacuoles are existing teaching markers associated with colloid scallops, not independently animated objects and not a complete modeled endocytic pathway.
Enlarged cell pitch, basal lamina and parathyroid cells preserve the original teaching layout; molecular callouts have no model-unit size.
Cell height and colloid morphology are activity cues, not sufficient evidence of hormone output or a diagnosis. Geometry never changes during playback.
Pre refine and Post refine require separate runtime instances bound to their independently verified artifact digests. Variant selection belongs to the root application.
thyroid_parathyroid_review_v2 is a distinct frozen model and is deliberately rejected by this hook.

Separate displayed cell rims and narrow teaching clefts do not depict a physiological leak. Follicular epithelium is taught as a sealed polarized barrier; iodide uptake and hormone release cross cells, not display gaps.

steps.title: Closed follicular unit
steps.caption: Polarized follicular epithelium surrounds a colloid lumen; the basal face meets supporting tissue and nearby capillaries.

steps.title: Separate parathyroid context
steps.caption: The original corner sample has its own capsule, chief-cell cords, oxyphil cells, fat and capillary sample.

steps.title: C-cell contextual identity
steps.caption: C cells are distinct from follicular cells and parathyroid chief cells; their product is calcitonin.

steps.title: Basal iodide uptake
steps.caption: Blood supplies iodide; NIS imports it across the blood-facing basolateral follicular-cell membrane. TSH regulates synthesis and release.

steps.title: Apical thyroglobulin supply
steps.caption: Follicular cells synthesize thyroglobulin and secrete it apically into the follicular lumen.

steps.title: Apical iodide delivery
steps.caption: Iodide crosses the apical membrane toward the lumen; no exclusive transporter assignment is implied.

steps.title: Apical iodination
steps.caption: At the apical-colloid boundary, TPO with peroxide iodinates thyroglobulin tyrosines into MIT and DIT.

steps.title: Coupling on thyroglobulin
steps.caption: Coupling on thyroglobulin forms T4 from DIT+DIT and T3 from MIT+DIT.
steps.compartment: apical-lumen boundary; hormone residues remain on thyroglobulin

steps.title: Extracellular colloid storage
steps.caption: Colloid stores hormone-containing thyroglobulin extracellularly; these are bound hormone residues, not a free-hormone pool.
steps.compartment: follicular lumen extracellular to the epithelium

steps.title: Apical colloid retrieval
steps.caption: Apical endocytosis retrieves colloid; the scallop markers identify resorption rather than circulating particles.

steps.title: Lysosomal hormone liberation
steps.caption: Intracellular lysosomal proteolysis liberates T4/T3; lysosomes are explained here without claiming a modeled organelle.
steps.compartment: intracellular lysosomal processing; text-only organelle cue

steps.title: Basal thyroid-hormone release
steps.caption: Free thyroid hormones leave basally toward nearby capillaries; the illustrated trunks do not form a proven route.

steps.title: Low extracellular calcium
steps.caption: Lower ionized calcium means less CaSR activation in parathyroid chief cells, permitting increased PTH secretion.
steps.compartment: chief-cell surface exposed to extracellular fluid

steps.title: PTH into nearby capillaries
steps.caption: Chief cells release PTH toward their own capillaries; this capillary is a separate representative vascular sample.

steps.title: PTH target-organ effects
steps.caption: Off-model targets: renal calcium retention, phosphate excretion, calcitriol production and bone remodeling help restore calcium.
steps.compartment: kidney and bone are described off-model; no physical routes

steps.title: Calcium feedback suppresses PTH
steps.caption: Rising extracellular calcium increases CaSR activation and suppresses PTH release; no dose-response curve is simulated.

steps.title: C cells secrete calcitonin
steps.caption: Elevated calcium can stimulate calcitonin release from thyroid C cells. This does not use colloid storage or iodinated thyroglobulin.

steps.title: Calcitonin physiological scope
steps.caption: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast-mediated resorption; its normal adult human calcium-homeostasis role is smaller than PTH/vitamin D.

lumen_domains.route: No duct or vascular luminal connection

lumen_domains.host_exclusion: Reserve complete outer vessel envelope, not wall alone
lumen_domains.connectivity: Each basket is an anastomosing graph; no global connection to displayed trunks is authored
